context: Each square represents one operation. The root is level 1. The top label reads “Recursion tree: each node branches in two,” and a brace on the right reads “n levels,” where n is a positive integer.
description: The first three levels have 1, 2, and 4 nodes. Each nonterminal node connects to two children. Below level 3, eight arrows lead to ellipses. Eight squares separated by ellipses illustrate the last level. Its node count is not fixed at eight. The right column gives the counts as powers, and the table also gives their decimal values for the first few levels. For n ≤ 3, use only the levels that exist. Row n then coincides with the corresponding earlier row.

frames.explanation: At the bottom, the counts sum to 2⁰ + 2¹ + … + 2ⁿ⁻¹ = 2ⁿ − 1, or two to the power n minus one, giving O(2ⁿ). In the cell division loop before the figure, level k represents the divisions performed by individual cells in round k. Over n rounds there are 2ⁿ − 1 divisions, leaving 2ⁿ cells. Those final cells are not drawn as another level of operations. For exp_recur(n) after the figure, each square represents one call. The argument decreases from n to 1 over n levels. Counting one per call gives the same total.
frames.title: A recursion tree that branches in two at each level

summary: The node count doubles at each successive level. To find the total work, sum the counts across levels.
